questions.question: A drum contains 40 litres of milk. One-fourth of the milk is taken out and replaced with water. Then, half of the mixture is taken out and replaced with water. What is the respective quantity of milk and water left in the drum?
questions.solution:
A drum contains 40 litres of milk.

One-fourth of the milk is taken out and replaced with water. 

One-fourth of the milk = 1/4 × 40 litres

One-fourth of the milk = 10 litres

Milk left in drum is = (40 - 10) = 30 litres 

And 10 litres of water was added.

Half of the mixture is taken out and replaced with water. 

Half of 30 litres milk = 1/2 × 30 = 15 litres

And 15 litres of water was added.

The respective quantity of:

Milk left in the drum = (30 - 15) = 15 litres

Water left in the drum = (10 + 15) = 25 litres

Hence, '**15 litres and 25 litres**’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: In which group of the modern periodic table are halogens placed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**17th.**__

__
 
• The Halogens are the elements belonging to Group** 17__** in the periodic table.

__
 
• A periodic table is an arrangement of elements based on their atomic numbers and chemical properties.
 
• It is divided into 18 groups and 7 periods running vertically and horizontally respectively.
 
• The periodic table accommodates a discrete combination of metal, non-metals, and metalloids.
 
• The elements in the periodic table are arranged horizontally in ascending order of their atomic numbers known as periods.
 
• Vertically the elements having identical chemical properties are clubbed together known as groups.
 
• The 18 groups are also known as columns and the 7 periods are also known as the rows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d16a8368d409900ed90309e3e688edcd632301cf42a7b2027cd2c23c0712d711.png] 

Explanation:__

Periods:

__
 
• Elements are arranged in increasing the atomic number of elements in a period.
 
• One extra electron gets added to the outermost shell as we move along the periods from left to right.
 
• The electron gets added to the same shell or orbit and thus the electrons present for bonding increase by one unit.
 
• Thus, the shell number remains the same but the number of electrons present for bonding increases along a period.

Groups:

 
• Elements having the same number of outer electrons are put in the same group of the periodic table.
 
• When we move down a group, new shells get added.
 
• The outermost shell has electrons present for bonding.
 
• Though the number of shells increases as we go down in a group, the number of electrons in the outermost shell remains the same.
 
• For example, the Halogens F, Cl, Br, I, At all belong to group 17 and have 7 electrons in the outermost shell.
 
• Similarly, Group 16 elements have 6 electrons in the outermost shell, group 15 has 5 electrons in the outermost shell, and so on.

• The digestive system of humans consists of the mouth, buccal cavity, pharynx, **oesophagus**, stomach, **small intestine, large intestine,** rectum, anus, and associated digestive glands.
 
• Digestion begins in the **mouth.**
 
• **The oesophagus** is the part that connects the mouth to the stomach.
 
 
• Protein digestion takes place in the **Stomach.**
 
• Simple sugars, alcohol, and medicines are absorbed in the stomach.
 
 
 
• The nutrients in digested food are absorbed from the **small intestine.**
 
• Maximum absorption occurs in the small intestine.

• The trench was named after the Mariana Islands which in turn were named after the **Queen Mariana of Austria **(widow of **Philip IV of Spain**) and the trench was declared as a **US National Monument in the year 2009**.

questions.question: A & B together do a work in 40 days. B & C together do in 25 days. A and B started working together, and A left work after 6 days & B left work after 8 days. After A left, C join the work & C completed the work in 40.5 days, C alone can complete the work in how many days?

Total work = 6 days of A + 8 days of B + 40.5 days of C = 1

⇒ Regrouping days: 6 days of (A + B) + 2 days of (B + C) + 38.5 days of C = 1

⇒ 6 × (1/40) + 2 × (1/25) + 38.5/C = 1

⇒ 3/20 + 2/25 + 38.5/C = 1 ⇒ 23/100 + 38.5/C = 1

⇒ 38.5/C = 77/100 ⇒ C = 3850 ÷ 77 = 50 days

**∴ The correct answer is 50 days.**

**Given:**

Time taken by (A + B) to complete the work = 40 days

Time taken by (B + C) to complete the work = 25 days

⇒ Total work = 6 days of (A + B) + 2 days of (B + C) + 38.5 days of C alone

⇒ Work done by (A + B) in 6 days = 6 × 5 = 30 units

By Alligation, Ratio of parts = (21.48 − 21) : (22 − 21.48) = 0.48 : 0.52 = 12 : 13.

Total ratio parts = 12 + 13 = 25 parts → ₹25,000.

Sum invested on SI (12 parts) = 12 × 1000 = ₹12,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total sum = ₹25,000

Rate for Part 1 (SI) = 11% p.a., Time = 2 years

Rate for Part 2 (CI) = 10% p.a., Time = 2 years

Total interest received = ₹5,370

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

CI Effective Rate = R + R + (R × R) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b3a58df1b05dbc284e5c19aa25efc7538dbf2dcfa1d0138d4f7557dcdec72c53.png]

⇒ Let the sum invested on SI be ₹x.

⇒ The sum invested on CI will be ₹(25000 − x).

questions.question: The population of a town increases annually by 25%. If the present population is one crore, then what is the difference between the population 3 years ago and 2 years ago?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Multiplying factor for a 25% annual increase is 1 + 1/4 = 5/4.

To find the past population, we multiply the current population by the reverse factor, which is 4/5.

Population 2 years ago = 1,00,00,000 × (4/5)² = 64,00,000.

Population 3 years ago = 64,00,000 × (4/5) = 51,20,000.

Required difference = 64,00,000 − 51,20,000 = 12,80,000.

**∴ The correct answer is 12,80,000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Present Population (P₀) = 1,00,00,000

Annual increase rate (R) = 25% = 1/4

**Formula Used:**

Past Population = Present Population × [1 / (1 + R)]ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2908c3e0e7ff741f1fa126e679a8cf5f62974b7541a5a4ab9b9ad8b28bcab411.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Multiplier for past population = 1 / (1 + 1/4) = 4/5

Population 2 years ago (P₂):

⇒ P₂ = 1,00,00,000 × (4/5)²

⇒ P₂ = 1,00,00,000 × 16/25 = 64,00,000

Population 3 years ago (P₃):

⇒ P₃ = 64,00,000 × (4/5)

⇒ P₃ = 51,20,000

Difference between the population 3 years ago and 2 years ago:

⇒ Difference = P₂ − P₃

⇒ Difference = 64,00,000 − 51,20,000 = 12,80,000

**∴ The correct answer is 12,80,000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Population Growth Formula

If a population grows at R% annually, the population after 'n' years is given by P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ.

Population Decay Formula

If a town's population decreases by R% annually, the population after 'n' years is given by P × (1 − R/100)ⁿ.

Successive Percentage Change

If the population changes by A%, B%, and C% in three successive years, the final population is P × (1 ± A/100) × (1 ± B/100) × (1 ± C/100).

Finding Past Population

To find the population 'n' years ago when the present population 'P' and growth rate 'R' are known: Past Population = P ÷ (1 + R/100)ⁿ.

questions.question: An article was sold by two shopkeepers at a total gain of 24%. If the first shopkeeper sold it at a gain of 6%, how much gain percentage did the second shopkeeper have?

Use the successive percentage change formula: Total Gain % = a + b + (a × b) / 100

Here, the Total Gain = 24%, the First Gain (a) = 6%, and let the Second Gain be b%.

⇒ 24 = 6 + b + (6 × b) / 100

⇒ 18 = 1.06b

⇒ b = 1800 / 106 = 900 / 53 = 16 52/53%

**∴ The correct answer is 16 52/53%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total gain percentage = 24%

Gain percentage of the first shopkeeper = 6%

**Calculations:**

Let the original Cost Price (CP) of the article be 100 units.

⇒ Selling Price for the first shopkeeper = 100 + (6% of 100) = 106 units.

The Selling Price of the first shopkeeper becomes the Cost Price (CP2) for the second shopkeeper.

⇒ Final Selling Price (SP) of the article after the overall 24% gain = 100 + (24% of 100) = 124 units.

⇒ Gain of the second shopkeeper = Final SP − CP for the second shopkeeper

⇒ Gain = 124 − 106 = 18 units.

⇒ Gain % of the second shopkeeper = (Gain ÷ CP for the second shopkeeper) × 100

⇒ Gain % = (18 / 106) × 100

⇒ Gain % = (9 / 53) × 100 = 900 / 53%

⇒ Gain % = 16 52/53%

**∴ The correct answer is 16 52/53%.**

Successive Profit

When an article is sold consecutively by multiple people, the overall profit is determined by successive percentage changes. The net profit of two successive gains x% and y% is given by the formula: (x + y + x×y / 100)%.

Cost Price & Selling Price Relation

Selling Price (SP) is calculated as: SP = CP × (100 + Gain%) ÷ 100. In a chain transaction, the Selling Price of one seller automatically acts as the Cost Price for the next buyer.

questions.question: Find the greatest possible number which on dividing 2307 and 3105 leaves remainders of 7 and 5 respectively.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The required greatest number is the HCF of the numbers obtained after subtracting the respective remainders.

Required Number = HCF of (2307 − 7) and (3105 − 5)

Required Number = HCF of 2300 and 3100

Both 2300 and 3100 are directly divisible by 100, and 23 and 31 are co-prime.

**∴ The correct answer is 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Dividend numbers = 2307 and 3105

Respective remainders = 7 and 5

**Formula Used:**

The greatest number that divides x and y leaving remainders a and b respectively is given by the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of (x − a) and (y − b).

**Calculations:**

⇒ First resulting number = 2307 − 7 = 2300

⇒ Second resulting number = 3105 − 5 = 3100

⇒ Now, find the prime factorization of 2300 and 3100:

⇒ 2300 = 23 × 100 = 23 × 2² × 5²

⇒ 3100 = 31 × 100 = 31 × 2² × 5²

⇒ The common factors between the two prime factorizations are 2² and 5².

⇒ HCF = 2² × 5²

⇒ HCF = 4 × 25 = 100

**∴ The correct answer is 100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Greatest Number Dividing with Specific Remainders

The greatest number that will divide x, y, and z leaving individual remainders a, b, and c respectively is given by finding the HCF of (x − a), (y − b), and (z − c).

Greatest Number Dividing with Same Remainder

The greatest number that will divide x, y, and z leaving the exact same remainder 'r' in each case is given by finding the HCF of (x − r), (y − r), and (z − r).

Greatest Number Dividing with Unknown Same Remainder

When x, y, and z are divided by the greatest number leaving the same but unknown remainder, the required number is the HCF of the absolute differences: |x − y|, |y − z|, and |z − x|.

Product Rule of LCM and HCF

For any two numbers 'A' and 'B', the product of the given numbers is strictly equal to the product of their LCM and HCF. Rule: A × B = LCM(A, B) × HCF(A, B).

questions.question: In a four-sided field the longer diagonal is 96 m. The lengths of perpendiculars from the opposite vertices 12 m and 8 m respectively. Find the area of the field.

Area of Rhombus

The area of a rhombus can be calculated primarily using its diagonals: Area = 1/2 × d₁ × d₂, where d₁ and d₂ are the lengths of the diagonals.

Area of Trapezium

The area of a trapezium is evaluated by considering its parallel sides: Area = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × (Perpendicular distance between them).

Heron's Formula

For any general triangle with side lengths a, b, and c, the area is √[s × (s − a) × (s − b) × (s − c)], where semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c)/2.

questions.question: Two wires of lengths 10 m 54 cm and 11 m 56 cm are both cut into pieces of length x cm each, where x is an integer. Find the maximum value of x.
questions.solution:

Convert the lengths to cm: 1054 cm and 1156 cm.

To find the maximum equal piece length x, calculate the HCF of 1054 and 1156.

Difference between the numbers = 1156 − 1054 = 102.

The HCF must be a factor of the difference (102). Factors of 102 are 102, 51, 34, 17, etc.

Both numbers are even and not divisible by 102. Checking 34: 1054 ÷ 34 = 31 and 1156 ÷ 34 = 34.

**∴ The correct answer is 34 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of second wire = 11 m 56 cm = 1100 cm + 56 cm = 1156 cm

Both wires are cut into pieces of length x cm. For x to be maximum, x must be the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of 1054 and 1156.

**Calculations:**

We will use the prime factorization method to find the HCF.

⇒ 1054 = 2 × 17 × 31

⇒ 1156 = 2 × 2 × 17 × 17

The common prime factors between the two numbers are 2 and 17.

⇒ HCF = 2 × 17 = 34

⇒ The maximum possible integer value of x is 34.

**∴ The correct answer is 34 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF Application

HCF is used when we need to split things into smaller, perfectly equal sections without leaving any remainder, or when trying to find the maximum possible length, weight, or size.

Difference Method for HCF

The HCF of two numbers is always either the absolute difference between the numbers or a factor of that difference. This is a powerful shortcut for exam problems.

Prime Factorization Method

Express each number as a product of prime numbers. The HCF is the product of the lowest powers of all common prime factors shared between the numbers.

questions.question: To travel from Patna to Gaya, Rupam takes 44 minutes more than Vikram. If Rupam increases his speed to 1.5 times then it may take 22 minutes less than Vikram. The distance between Patna to Gaya is 132 km Then find the average time taken by Rupam and Vikram to cover the distance from Patna to Gaya.

Ratio of Rupam's original speed to new speed = 1 : 1.5 = 2 : 3, so time ratio = 3 : 2.

Difference in time ratio = 3 − 2 = 1 part.

Actual time difference due to speed change = 44 − (−22) = 66 mins.

Rupam's time (3 parts) = 3 × 66 = 198 mins; Vikram's time = 198 − 44 = 154 mins.

Average time = (198 + 154) ÷ 2 = 176 mins = 176 ÷ 60 ≈ 2.94 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.94 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Largest number = 37 × 17 = 629

**∴ The correct answer is 629.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

H.C.F. of the two numbers = 37

Other two divisors of their L.C.M. = 15 and 17

**Formula Used:**

L.C.M. of two numbers = H.C.F. × a × b (where a and b are the non-common co-prime factors)

The two numbers can be represented as (H.C.F. × a) and (H.C.F. × b).

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the non-common co-prime factors of the L.C.M. be a = 15 and b = 17.

⇒ The first number = H.C.F. × a

⇒ First number = 37 × 15 = 555

⇒ The second number = H.C.F. × b

⇒ Second number = 37 × 17 = 629

⇒ Comparing the two numbers, 629 > 555.

⇒ The largest number among them is 629.

**∴ The correct answer is 629.**

Product of Two Numbers

The product of any two numbers is always equal to the product of their H.C.F. and L.C.M. Formula: Number 1 × Number 2 = H.C.F. × L.C.M.

Co-prime Factors

When the L.C.M. is divided by the H.C.F., the resulting quotient is the product of two co-prime numbers, which effectively act as the simplest ratio parts of the two numbers.

Finding L.C.M. from H.C.F. and Ratios

If two numbers are in the ratio a : b and their H.C.F. is H, then their L.C.M. can be directly calculated as H × a × b.

questions.question: The parallel sides of a trapezium are 20 cm and 10cm and its non-parallel sides are equal to each other. If its area is 180cm², then what is the length (in cm) of each non-parallel side?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Height of trapezium = (2 × Area) ÷ Sum of parallel sides = (2 × 180) ÷ (20 + 10) = 12 cm.

Base of the right-angled triangle formed at the ends = (20 − 10) ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

Length of each non-parallel side = √(12² + 5²) = √(144 + 25) = √169 = 13 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Parallel sides of the trapezium are 20 cm and 10 cm.

Area of the isosceles trapezium = 180 cm².

**Formula Used:**

Area of Trapezium = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d4e4a71f0642676412bd6d0f0c293bd1a28315e8d77aaf2fcc2457de5b0b5a82.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = 1/2 × (AB + CD) × Height

⇒ 180 = 1/2 × (10 + 20) × h

⇒ 180 = 1/2 × 30 × h

⇒ 180 = 15 × h

⇒ h = 12 cm

So, the height of the trapezium (AM = BN) is 12 cm.

In isosceles trapezium ABCD, dropping perpendiculars AM and BN to CD constructs a rectangle ABMN.

⇒ MN = AB = 10 cm

Since it is an isosceles trapezium, the remaining base segments are equal:

⇒ DM = NC = (CD − MN) ÷ 2

⇒ DM = (20 − 10) ÷ 2 = 5 cm

Now, applying Pythagoras theorem in right-angled ΔAMD:

⇒ AD² = AM² + DM²

⇒ AD² = 12² + 5²

⇒ AD = √(144 + 25)

⇒ AD = √169 = 13 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 13 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Isosceles Trapezium Properties

In an isosceles trapezium, the non-parallel sides are equal in length, the base angles are equal, and the lengths of the diagonals are identical.

Area of a Trapezium

The area is calculated as Area = 1/2 × (a + b) × h, where 'a' and 'b' are the lengths of the parallel sides and 'h' is the perpendicular distance (height) between them.

Median of a Trapezium

The median is the line segment joining the midpoints of the non-parallel sides. Its length is the average of the parallel sides: m = (a + b) ÷ 2, and Area = m × h.
</p

questions.question: A fruit seller sells mangoes at the rate of Rs. 7 per kg and thereby loses 20%. At what price per kg he should have sold them to make a profit of 4%?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Using the Direct Percentage Equivalence method:

At 20% loss, Selling Price = 80% of CP = Rs. 7

For 4% profit, required Selling Price = 104% of CP

New SP = 7 × (104 ÷ 80) = 7 × 1.3 = 9.1

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 9.1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = Rs. 7

Loss Percentage (L%) = 20%

Desired Profit Percentage (P%) = 4%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP₁ × [100 ÷ (100 − L%)]

New Selling Price (SP₂) = CP × [(100 + P%) ÷ 100]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6fa56fd4a24023ff9b86624b6d3e2e46fc01b091ed65d35a008ce69a94bc7c74.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP = 7 × [100 ÷ (100 − 20)]

⇒ CP = 7 × (100 ÷ 80)

⇒ CP = 7 × 1.25 = Rs. 8.75

⇒ To achieve a 4% profit, SP₂ = 8.75 × [(100 + 4) ÷ 100]

⇒ SP₂ = 8.75 × 1.04

⇒ SP₂ = Rs. 9.1

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 9.1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Equivalent Percentage Method

When selling items at different profit/loss percentages on the same cost base, the ratio of Selling Prices directly matches their percentage equivalents: SP₁ ÷ SP₂ = (100 − L%) ÷ (100 + P%).

Marked Price & Discount Relation

Selling Price is also found using Marked Price (MP) and Discount (D%): SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100. The relationship between MP and CP simplifies to: MP ÷ CP = (100 + P%) ÷ (100 − D%).

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer claims to sell at Cost Price but uses a lesser false weight, the actual Profit% = [Error ÷ (True Weight − Error)] × 100.
</p

Total Work Concept

Total Work is universally assumed as the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of the individual times. This makes the calculation of daily efficiency an integer value, which significantly simplifies further calculations.

questions.question: A man travelled a distance of 47 km in 6 hours. He travelled partly on foot at a speed of 6(1)/(2) km/h and the rest on bicycle at a speed of 8(1)/(2) km/h. The distance travelled (in km) on bicycle is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the Alligation method on speeds to find the time ratio:

Average speed = 47/6 km/h | Foot speed = 13/2 = 39/6 km/h | Bicycle speed = 17/2 = 51/6 km/h

Time Ratio (Foot : Bicycle) = (51/6 − 47/6) : (47/6 − 39/6) = 4/6 : 8/6 = 1 : 2

Total time = 6 hours → Time spent on bicycle = (2/3) × 6 = 4 hours

Distance travelled on bicycle = Speed × Time = 8.5 × 4 = 34 km

**∴ The correct answer is 34 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 47 km

Total time = 6 hours

Speed on foot = 6.5 km/h

Speed on bicycle = 8.5 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9d01cac8c561670f583d1b1ceb19007bfef1e8b63229ad60229e49ec751bdb68.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

Let the time travelled on foot be t hours.

⇒ Time travelled on bicycle = (6 − t) hours.

⇒ Distance travelled on foot = 6.5 × t

⇒ Distance travelled on bicycle = 8.5 × (6 − t)

⇒ Total distance = 6.5t + 8.5(6 − t)

⇒ 6.5t + 51 − 8.5t = 47

⇒ 51 − 47 = 8.5t − 6.5t

⇒ 4 = 2t

⇒ t = 2 hours

So, the time spent on the bicycle is 6 − 2 = 4 hours.

⇒ Distance travelled on bicycle = 8.5 × 4 = 34 km

**∴ The correct answer is 34 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If a journey is split into two equal distances travelled at speeds S₁ and S₂, then Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Alligation on Speed

When the rule of alligation is applied to the speeds of two parts of a journey, the resulting ratio represents the ratio of the time taken for those parts, not the ratio of distances.

Relative Speed

If two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their speeds (S₁ − S₂). If they move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their speeds (S₁ + S₂).
</p

• The conjunction 'nor' is used **to indicate a negative state that continues after something else negative happens**.
